title: Testora: Regression Testing with a Natural Language Oracle
summary: The original Testora pipeline detects behavioral regressions introduced by pull requests through a three-stage process: (1) test generation — an LLM generates Python test cases that exercise the changed code, (2) test execution — generated tests are run against the pre-PR and post-PR commits inside isolated Docker containers, and (3) classification — a second LLM call compares the actual execution outputs and classifies the behavioral difference as intended or unintended. The pipeline uses GPT-4o-mini in a multi-question prompting strategy and evaluates on 46 manually labeled PRs (RQ3) and 30 real-world problems detected in the wild (RQ1).

This reproduction replaces the full three-stage pipeline with a single Claude Sonnet 4.6 call. Given the PR metadata (title, description, diff, commit messages, discussion comments), the model is asked in one shot to: generate a test case, predict its output before and after the PR, and classify the behavioral change as intended or unintended. Two prompt strategies are compared: Prompt A (black-box, no methodology guidance) and Prompt B (step-by-step, with 7 explicit reasoning steps from diff parsing to verdict).
